doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Going solo and the Dizzy Gillespie years
title: The Floating Jazz Festival CD with Joe Temperley
summary: Rowe praises the CD; they discuss Temperley's baritone sound and bass clarinet on selected tunes.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah. I have that CD you mentioned.
I love that version you do of “In a Sentimental Mood” with him way up high on the baritone.
Right. Doesn’t he get a great sound?
Yeah. It’s not harsh or coarse like a lot of baritones can sound that get up there.
It almost sounds like a Joe Williams singing falsetto or something.

Right, yeah. Yeah and we also do a thing on there where he does bass clarinet I think, we do the medley of “Single Petal of a Rose” and “Sunset and Mockingbird.” On “Single Petal of a Rose” he plays that on the bass clarinet.
